question.text: A string passes over a pulley fixed to a ceiling support. One end of this string holds a 4 kg block. The other end holds a 3 kg block, and a second string ties a 1 kg block below that 3 kg block. Work out the ratio of the tension in the string holding the 4 kg block to the tension in the string holding the 1 kg block.
conditions: pulley is fixed to the ceiling
4 kg block hangs from one end of the string over the pulley
3 kg block hangs from the other end of the string over the pulley
1 kg block hangs below the 3 kg block, tied to it by a second string

figure.description: A pulley hangs fixed from a ceiling support. A string runs over this pulley: its left end carries a 4 kg block, hanging straight down. Its right end carries a 3 kg block, also hanging straight down. A separate string then connects downward from the 3 kg block to a 1 kg block beneath it.

solution.approach: Since the total mass on each side of the pulley is equal, the system stays at rest, and each string tension equals the weight it directly supports.

steps.text: Add the masses on each side of the fixed pulley.
steps.equation: left side = 4 kg, right side = 3+1 = 4 kg

steps.text: Equal masses on each side mean the system has zero acceleration.
steps.why_this_step: With no acceleration, each string tension can be found from plain equilibrium instead of a full Atwood-machine equation.

steps.text: The tension in the string over the pulley, attached to the 4 kg block, supports the whole 4 kg block in equilibrium.
The tension in the string attached to the 1 kg block supports only the 1 kg block, since it hangs below the 3 kg block.
Take the ratio of the two tensions.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the system accelerates because the two sides look different, missing that 3 kg + 1 kg on the right equals the 4 kg on the left.
Taking the tension in the string attached to the 1 kg block as the same main tension over the pulley, instead of the smaller tension in the separate lower string.
